title_en: Xie Donghui and Zheng Zhaoben v. Chen Shijun et al. — inheritance dispute

full_text_en:
Xie Donghui, Zheng Zhaoben v. Chen Shijun et al. — dispute over inheritance

Plaintiffs: Xie Donghui, female, 50 years old.

Plaintiff: Zheng Zhaoben, male, 60 years old, husband of Xie Donghui.

The above plaintiffs reside at Huijiamiao Metallurgy Building, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.

Defendants: Chen Shijun, male, 43 years old.

Defendant: Chen Xiuying, female, 46 years old.

Defendant: Chen Ruiyu, female, 33 years old.

Defendant: Chen Shizhong, male, 37 years old.

The above defendants reside at Mengjiaxiang, Xi'an City, Shaanxi Province.

Plaintiffs Xie Donghui and Zheng Zhaoben filed a lawsuit with the Beilin District People's Court of Xi'an, Shaanxi Province, against defendants Chen Shijun, Chen Xiuying, Chen Ruiyu, and Chen Shizhong regarding a dispute over inheritance.

Plaintiffs Xie Donghui and Zheng Zhaoben alleged that their daughter Zheng Ping met the defendants' younger brother Chen Shijie through a friend in 1985, soon fell in love, and had a very good relationship. Starting from January 1987, Zheng Ping helped Chen Shijie with household chores and cohabited with him, until both were killed on April 11, 1989, thereby forming a de facto marital relationship. During this period, they worked together and purchased daily necessities such as a color TV, refrigerator, tape recorder, video recorder, and washing machine. They requested the court to rule that the plaintiffs inherit Zheng Ping's遗产 (estate) according to law.

Defendants Chen Shijun, Chen Xiuying, Chen Ruiyu, and Chen Shizhong argued that the plaintiffs' daughter did not register her marriage with their younger brother Chen Shijie before his death, thus it was not a lawful marital relationship, and their cohabitation was illegal. Now that both have been tragically killed, the property left behind is Chen Shijie's personal property, not community property. The plaintiffs have no right to inherit Chen Shijie's遗产 (estate).

After a public hearing, the Beilin District People's Court found: Plaintiffs Xie Donghui and Zheng Zhaoben are the parents of the decedent Zheng Ping. Defendants Chen Shijun, Chen Xiuying, Chen Ruiyu, and Chen Shizhong are the siblings of the decedent Chen Shijie. Starting from January 1987, Zheng Ping and Chen Shijie openly cohabited under the name of husband and wife and purchased household items. The above facts are confirmed by witness testimony, letters written by Chen Shijie before his death, and other documentary evidence. On the night of April 11, 1989, Zheng Ping and Chen Shijie were killed in their home. After the deaths of Zheng Ping and Chen Shijie, they left behind savings and cash of RMB 12,810, a creditor's right of RMB 10,000, two color TVs, one refrigerator, one washing machine, one radio-cassette recorder, one television projector, one electric fan, one gold necklace, and furniture and daily necessities. The above遗产 (estate) was inspected by the Xi'an Municipal Public Security Bureau and is currently in the custody of the defendants.

It was further found that Zheng Ping was a workshop accountant at Xi'an Silicate Products Factory, born on April 20, 1964, and was 23 years old when she began cohabiting with Chen Shijie, with no spouse. Chen Shijie was an individual industrial and commercial household, born on June 22, 1961, and was 26 years old when he began cohabiting with Zheng Ping, with no spouse. During their cohabitation, Zheng Ping and Chen Shijie had no children. Chen Shijie's father, Chen Xianmin, and mother, Wu Lanhua, passed away in 1977 and 1982, respectively.

The Beilin District People's Court held: According to Article 2 of the Supreme People's Court's "Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases of Cohabitation under the Name of Husband and Wife without Marriage Registration," after the implementation of the "Marriage Registration Measures" on March 15, 1986, cohabitation under the name of husband and wife without marriage registration may be recognized as a de facto marriage if both parties met the legal conditions for marriage at the time of cohabitation. Zheng Ping and Chen Shijie cohabited under the name of husband and wife without marriage registration for two years, and they met the legal conditions for marriage. Their marital relationship should be recognized as a de facto marriage. According to the above provisions, the property of Zheng Ping and Chen Shijie during cohabitation should be considered community property. Plaintiffs Xie Donghui and Zheng Zhaoben are the heirs of the decedent Zheng Ping, and in accordance with Article 10, Paragraph 1 of the Inheritance Law of the People's Republic of China, they have the right to inherit that portion of Zheng Ping's遗产 (estate). The parents of the decedent Chen Shijie are both deceased, and he had no children. In accordance with the above provisions, his遗产 (estate) should be inherited by the second-order heirs, Chen Shijun, Chen Xiuying, Chen Ruiyu, and Chen Shizhong. The defendants Chen Shijun, Chen Xiuying, Chen Ruiyu, and Chen Shizhong argued that all property in the household of Zheng Ping and Chen Shijie belonged solely to Chen Shijie, but the evidence was insufficient, and this claim was not upheld. Given that Zheng Ping and Chen Shijie cohabited for a short period and a significant portion of the community property belonged to Chen Shijie before cohabitation, his heirs should receive a appropriately larger share. Accordingly, on November 27, 1989, the Beilin District People's Court ruled:

Plaintiffs Xie Donghui and Zheng Zhaoben inherit the decedent Zheng Ping's遗产 (estate): a creditor's right of RMB 6,000, one "Sharp" 20-inch color TV, four quilt covers, and one towel blanket.

Defendants Chen Shijun, Chen Xiuying, Chen Ruiyu, and Chen Shizhong inherit the decedent Chen Shijie's遗产 (estate): RMB 16,810, a color TV, refrigerator, washing machine, electric fan, radio-cassette recorder, television projector, gold necklace, and over 30 items of daily use items.

After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, plaintiffs Xie Donghui and Zheng Zhaoben appealed to the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court of Shaanxi Province, arguing that the first-instance judgment's division of the遗产 (estate) of Zheng Ping and Chen Shijie was unreasonable and failed to reflect the principle of consistency between rights and obligations.

During the trial, the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court, in addition to the facts found in the first instance, further found that, according to the forensic medical examination conclusion issued by the public security organ regarding the time of death of Zheng Ping and Chen Shijie, Chen Shijie died approximately 20 minutes before Zheng Ping. It also found that after Zheng Ping and Chen Shijie were killed, the appellants Xie Donghui and Zheng Zhaoben jointly contributed to and hosted the funeral together with the appellees Chen Shijun and the other three, and the wreaths sent by the appellees referred to the victim Zheng Ping as "sister-in-law." Before his death, Chen Shijie owed RMB 1,000 to the appellee Chen Ruiyu, which remained unpaid.

The Xi'an Intermediate People's Court held: Zheng Ping and Chen Shijie openly lived under the name of husband and wife before their deaths, forming a de facto marriage, which should be regarded as a marital relationship, and their property should be community property. Article 2 of the Inheritance Law stipulates: "Succession begins at the death of the decedent." Article 10, Paragraph 2 stipulates: "In the inheritance of遗产 (estate), after the opening of succession, the first-order heirs inherit, and the second-order heirs do not inherit. Where there are no first-order heirs, the第二顺序继承人 (second-order heirs) inherit." Chen Shijie died approximately 20 minutes before Zheng Ping. According to the provisions of the Inheritance Law, upon Chen Shijie's death, his遗产 (estate) should be inherited by the first-order heir, Zheng Ping. Upon Zheng Ping's death, her遗产 (estate) should be inherited by the first-order heirs, i.e., the appellants Xie Donghui and Zheng Zhaoben in this case.

The debts left by Chen Shijie shall be satisfied by Xie Donghui and Zheng Zhaoben from the遗产 (estate) they inherit. Chen Shijun, Chen Xiuying, Chen Ruiyu, and Chen Shizhong are Chen Shijie's second-order statutory heirs and have no right to inherit Chen Shijie's遗产 (estate). However, the four appellees, Chen Shijun et al., provided some assistance to Chen Shijie during his lifetime and, together with the appellants, handled the funeral after the deaths of Chen Shijie and Zheng Ping. According to Article 14 of the Inheritance Law, they may be given an appropriate share of the遗产 (estate). The first-instance judgment had unclear factual findings and incorrect application of law, and should be amended according to law. Accordingly, on March 19, 1991, the court ruled:

1. The first-instance judgment is reversed.
2. The appellees Chen Shijun, Chen Xiuying, Chen Ruiyu, and Chen Shizhong are each awarded RMB 2,000.
3. The appellants Xie Donghui and Zheng Zhaoben inherit all remaining遗产 (estate).
4. The appellants Xie Donghui and Zheng Zhaoben shall, within one month after this judgment takes effect, make a one-time payment of RMB 1,000 owed by Chen Shijie to Chen Ruiyu.
